source.uploadedFile: Curriculum new LLB Hons. 1st & 2nd semester Batch -2023 (2).pdf
verificationNotes: This catalogue covers only Semesters 1 and 2 because the uploaded PDF contains those semesters only.
The Semester 2 overview table calls course LLB-202 Family Law-I, while the detailed syllabus section labels it Family Law-II. This discrepancy is preserved for verification.
The source uses legacy Indian Penal Code (IPC) section references in Law of Crimes-I. Verify current statutory applicability before using this syllabus for legal advice.

The University of Jammu publishes a separate revised three-year LL.B. syllabus for Semesters I–VI. Do not automatically merge that syllabus into this MIET LLB (Hons.) catalogue without confirming that it is the same programme and applicable scheme.
source.coverage: Six-semester structure; detailed syllabus currently available only for Semesters 1 and 2

units.title: Introduction to Legal Methods and Law
Sources of Law
topics: Juristic writings: justice, equity and good conscience
Stare decisis, res judicata, ratio decidendi and obiter dicta

units.title: Basic Principles of Indian Legal System
topics: Constitution as the law of the land
Salient features of the Indian Constitution

units.title: Judicial System in India
topics: Court jurisdiction: territorial, pecuniary and subject matter
Alternative dispute resolution: arbitration, negotiation, mediation and conciliation
Lok Adalat and Nyaya through Panchayati Raj Institutions

units.title: Introduction
topics: Constitution and constitutionalism: meaning and significance
Salient features of the Indian Constitution

units.title: Concept of State and Fundamental Rights
topics: Fundamental Rights: concept, origin and development
Meaning of law and laws in force (Article 13)
Doctrine of ultra vires, severability, eclipse and waiver

units.title: Fundamental Rights-I (Articles 14–22)
topics: Right to freedom and reasonable restrictions (Article 19)
Ex-post facto laws, double jeopardy and self-incrimination (Article 20)
Right to life and personal liberty (Article 21)
Protection against arrest and preventive detention (Article 22)

units.title: Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Duties
topics: Directive Principles of State Policy: nature and significance
Relationship and distinction between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs
Relationship between DPSPs and Fundamental Duties

units.title: General Principles of Contract
topics: Basic concepts: definition, nature, characteristics and types of contracts; agreement and standard-form contract
Acceptance: definition, nature, essentials, legal rules, communication and revocation

units.title: Consent (Sections 15–19)
topics: Coercion, undue influence, fraud and misrepresentation
Effects of coercion, undue influence, fraud and misrepresentation on contracts

units.title: Consideration
topics: Void, voidable and valid agreements: definitions
Agreements in restraint of marriage, trade and legal proceedings; uncertainty and wagering agreements

units.title: Performance of Contract
topics: Persons who must perform and obligations of parties
Time, place and manner of performance
Performance of reciprocal and alternative promises

subjects.name: Law of Torts including MV & CP Act

units.title: Introduction and Principles of Liability in Torts
topics: Nature, meaning and definitions of tort
General conditions of tortious liability and negating tortious liability
Distinction between tort, contract and crime
Injuria sine damnum and damnum sine injuria
Liability principles: fault, wrongful intent, negligence and liability without fault

units.title: Defences in Action for Tort
topics: Necessity, plaintiff’s default, act of God and inevitable accident
Private defence, statutory authority, judicial and quasi-judicial acts

units.title: Torts against Persons and Torts Affecting Property
topics: Assault, battery, false imprisonment and malicious prosecution
Negligence: standards and duty of care, carelessness, contributory negligence and res ipsa loquitur

units.title: Strict and Vicarious Liability
topics: Vicarious liability: basis, scope and justification
Special relationships: master and servant; control test
Independent contractor and servant; principal and agent; sovereign immunity
Strict liability: rule in Rylands v. Fletcher and harm caused by dangerous industries
Absolute liability: rule in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India

units.title: Consumer Protection and Motor Vehicle Laws
topics: Consumer Protection Act, 2019: objectives, definitions and salient features
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988: objectives and salient features

units.title: Environmental Protection: International and National Perspective
topics: Precautionary principle, polluter-pays principle and public-trust doctrine

units.title: Constitutional Guidelines
topics: Right to wholesome environment: evolution and application

units.title: Prevention and Control of Water, Air, Noise and Land Pollution
topics: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974; pollution control boards, control areas, sampling and consent procedure
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981; pollution control boards, control areas and consent procedure

units.title: General Environmental Legislations and Protection of Forests and Wildlife
topics: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; definitions, Central Government powers and functions
Notifications under Section 6 and hazardous-substance regulation
Forest Act, 1927 and categories of forests
Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 and forest conservation vis-à-vis tribal rights
Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972: authorities, hunting, specified plants, protected areas and trade prohibition

units.title: Tribunals
topics: National Green Tribunal: functions and powers

units.title: Course activities listed in the syllabus
topics: Business manners: handshake, gifts, visiting cards, humour and office behaviour
Power dressing, wardrobe etiquette and grooming
Body language, poise and eye contact
Preparing effective presentations with modern tools
Art of entertaining and being a gracious host
Self-grooming, personal hygiene, gestures and postures
Language lab: vocabulary, punctuation, verbal/non-verbal communication, confidence, assertive communication, persuasion and asking questions

units.title: Legal Database Lab activities
topics: Primary and secondary sources of law
Overview of statutes, bills, case laws, journals, commentaries, digests, manuals and dictionaries
Use of online databases and e-resources for legislation, articles and case laws
Navigate legal databases including Legal Eagle, Manupatra, SCC Online and journals
Citation patterns, footnotes, endnotes and bibliography

units.title: Induction training activities
topics: ICT tools: official email, Google Drive, Google Classroom and Google Meet
Project showcasing: AI, computer vision and RPA
Orientation to NSS and cultural committees

units.title: Executive and Legislature under Indian Constitution
topics: Council of Ministers: election, powers and functions; Governor: appointment, powers and functions
State Government and Cabinet; power to make laws
Union and State Legislatures: composition, powers, functions and privileges
Bills, joint sitting, Money Bills and budget

units.title: Judiciary under Constitution
topics: Supreme Court: establishment, composition, appointment of judges, powers and jurisdiction
Appointment and transfer of judges; powers and jurisdiction
Subordinate judiciary, judicial independence and accountability; writ jurisdiction

units.title: Centre-State Relations
topics: Cooperation and coordination between Centre and States

units.title: Liability of State in Torts and Contracts (as titled in source)
Elections, Emergency and Amendment
topics: Election Commission: composition, powers and functions
Superintendence of elections, anti-defection law and Representation of the People Act, 1951
Impact of emergency on federalism and Fundamental Rights
Amendment of the Indian Constitution: power and procedure

subjects.name: Family Law-I / Family Law-II (source discrepancy)
subjects.verificationNote: Semester 2 overview table lists Family Law-I; the detailed syllabus page labels the course Family Law-II. The units below are transcribed from the detailed syllabus section.

units.title: Introduction to Hindu and Muslim Law
topics: Concept and importance of Family Law in India
Origin and sources of Hindu Law
Origin and sources of Muslim Law
Schools of Hindu Law: Mitakshara and Dayabhaga
Schools of Muslim Law: Sunni, Shia and other schools

units.title: Laws regarding Marriage under Hindu and Muslim Law
topics: Evolution and concept of the institution of marriage
Definition, object and nature of Nikah
Recent trends in marriage; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and Amendment Act, 1976

units.title: Dissolution of Marriage and Matrimonial Relief
topics: Grounds of divorce under Hindu and Muslim Law
Divorce by mutual consent under Hindu and Muslim Law
Restitution of conjugal rights under Hindu and Muslim Law

units.title: Maintenance under Hindu and Muslim Law
topics: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986
Maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (as named in source)

units.title: Laws of Adoption and Guardianship under Hindu and Muslim Law
topics: Capability, necessary conditions and effects of adoption
Guardianship under Hindu and Muslim Law
Secular concept of adoption under Juvenile Justice Act, 2015

units.title: Introduction to International Law
topics: Definition and nature of international law
Origin and basis of international law
Relationship between international and municipal law

units.title: State
topics: States as subjects of international law
Law of the sea: territorial waters, contiguous zone, high seas, continental shelf and EEZ

units.title: International Organisations
topics: United Nations: objectives, principles and membership
Security Council and General Assembly: composition, functions and powers; ECOSOC
World Trade Organization: purpose and functions

units.title: Indemnity and Guarantee
topics: Contract of indemnity and guarantee: definition and nature (Sections 124 and 126)
Rights of indemnity holder and guarantor (Sections 125 and 127–129)

units.title: Bailment and Pledge
topics: Bailment and pledge: definition and nature (Sections 148 and 172)
Rights of bailor, bailee, pawnor and pawnee (sections as cited in source)
Finder of goods as a bailee (Sections 168–169)
Pawnee’s right of sale (source cites Section 172)

units.title: The Sale of Goods Act, 1930
topics: Meaning and essentials of contract of sale and goods (Sections 4 and 6–8)

units.title: Introduction
topics: Historical perspective and introduction to Civil Procedure Code
Decree, judgement, order, foreign court/judgement, mesne profits, affidavit, suit, plaint and written statement
Res sub judice, res judicata, restitution, caveat and inherent powers of courts

units.title: Initial Steps in a Suit
topics: Pleadings: meaning, object, general rules and amendment

units.title: Limitation Act, 1963
topics: Historical background of the Limitation Act
Limitation of suits, appeals and applications (Sections 3–5)

units.title: Introduction to Substantive Criminal Law
topics: Distinction between crime and other wrongs
Elements of crime: actus reus and mens rea

units.title: General Exceptions (Sections 76–106, as cited in source)
topics: Private defence of body and property (Sections 96–106)

units.title: Offences Relating to Human Body
topics: Causing death by negligence and dowry death (Sections 304-A and 304-B)

units.title: Offences against State and Property
topics: Offences against the State and sedition (sections cited in source: 121 and 124)
Criminal misappropriation and criminal breach of trust

units.title: Academic Report Writing
topics: Footnotes, references, bibliography, indexes and appendices

units.title: Legal Maxims
topics: Latin and other foreign phrases used in legal writing
Meaning and importance of legal maxims
Origin and application of legal maxims

units.title: MOOC selection and assessment
topics: Select a 4–6 week MOOC from SWAYAM, NPTEL or another reputed platform
Obtain approval from the departmental committee
The selected course should not duplicate regular department courses
Assessment through a presentation/project and course-completion certificate
